title: The primary KPI tile sits top-left in DOM order and in CSS Grid position across the ratified breakpoints
asA: reader glancing at the shipped dashboard on a laptop, a tablet and a phone
iWant: the primary KPI to land at the top-left first-fixation position on every ratified breakpoint
soThat: the F-scan reading pattern lands on the primary KPI first, without a per-surface layout negotiation

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered dashboard surface at each of the three ratified viewports (1440, 1024, 360), the primary KPI tile (`data-tile-role="primary-kpi"`) is the first tile in DOM order within the tile row region; at 1440 and 1024 the tile's computed CSS Grid `grid-column-start` is 1 and `grid-row-start` is 1; at 360 the tile row reflows to one column and the primary KPI's `grid-row-start` is 1 (the top row). The tile carries a `data-kpi-kind` attribute whose value is one of the ADR-2001 enum (revenue, active-users, error-rate, throughput, custom). Probed by the application-dashboard pack check AC-19102-1 (Playwright drives the browser to the dashboard route, resizes the viewport to each of the three widths, reads the DOM order and the computed CSS Grid position, and asserts every breakpoint places the primary KPI top-left).
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered dashboard surface at 1440, 1024 and 360
acceptanceCriteria.when: the DOM order and the computed CSS Grid position are read
acceptanceCriteria.then: the primary KPI tile is first in DOM order and top-left in CSS Grid at each of the three widths

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered dashboard surface with no primary KPI tile, the surface either supersedes REQ-002 with a project-authored REQ documenting the omission or fails project-side review. This case is a documentation-and-review contract; the pack asserts the primary KPI tile exists (AC-19102-1) but does not itself enforce the fallback path.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered dashboard with no primary KPI tile
acceptanceCriteria.then: the surface supersedes REQ-002 with a project-authored REQ or fails review

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered dashboard at the 360 breakpoint, when the tile row reflows to one column, the primary KPI tile carries `row-start: 1` in its computed CSS Grid position; a secondary tile whose row-start is 1 at 360 (competing for the top-left slot) fails the pack check.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered dashboard at 360 with the tile row reflowed to one column
acceptanceCriteria.when: the pack inspects computed CSS Grid positions
acceptanceCriteria.then: the primary KPI tile has row-start: 1 and no secondary tile shares that row-start

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given the operator elicited `primary-kpi-kind=custom`, the primary tile carries `data-kpi-kind="custom"` AND a `data-kpi-name` attribute whose value is the operator-elicited `primary-kpi-custom-name`; a `custom` kind without a `data-kpi-name` fails the pack check. Applying agent sets: the custom short name.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered dashboard whose primary-kpi-kind is elicited as `custom`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the pack inspects the primary tile attributes
acceptanceCriteria.then: the tile carries both `data-kpi-kind="custom"` and a non-empty `data-kpi-name` matching the elicited short name

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered dashboard whose primary tile carries a `data-kpi-kind` value outside the ADR-2001 enum (a typo, an operator override that did not follow the elicit), the pack fails the check naming the invalid value; the check reads the attribute value and asserts membership in {revenue, active-users, error-rate, throughput, custom}.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a primary tile with a data-kpi-kind value outside the ADR-2001 enum
acceptanceCriteria.then: the check fails naming the invalid value and asserting the required enum membership
